acceptanceCriteria: Both consumers give identical outcome, stage, code, issueCodes and verdictSha256 for the dropped-hunk map, enforced by one shared sealed REJECT case run in internal/cem/verify and interop/cem01-go tests.
body:
Observed by the 2026-10-13 CEM 1.0 confidence panel (test-conformance lens). Take committed map e2212e55 (cem/1.0), delete one hunk from `hunks`, verify against an ABSENT-sidecar target (758e2f45).
Expected: CEM-V1-082/CEM-V1-09x require both consumers to give the same outcome, stage, code and verdictSha256.
Actual: native `corvint cem verify-stable` gives REJECT stage=wire code=invalid-field changeIntegrity=NOT_CHECKED verdictSha256=92279ac9...; portable `cem01 verify-stable-canonical` gives REJECT stage=verification code=null issueCodes=[invalid-field] changeIntegrity=FAILED verdictSha256=6c0f91c9.... Distinct from V1-1295 (partial drift list on UNSUPPORTED). No shared sealed case covers a dropped hunk; the packet has zero REJECT cases (R1-EXPECTED.json is DECLARATIVE_NOT_EXECUTED).
Repro inputs: panel/test-conf/tamper/10-hunk-dropped.json, n.*.out, p.*.out, mk.py.

title: cem verify: native and portable stable consumers diverge on a dropped-hunk map (stage, code, verdictSha256)
